sections.heading: C - Traffic Controls
sections.markdown:
## C - Traffic Controls

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Drivers hold their lane except to turn, exit, or shift, may briefly cross center for bikes and walkers, and read white edges right with yellow edges left on split roads [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
White divides same-way flows with broken lines changeable, solid lines avoided, and doubles never crossed, while yellow divides opposing flows with broken lines passable from the right [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A02
Double solid yellows bar all crossing except left turns and bike passes, solid-right pairs bar passing, and broken-right pairs permit it [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A03
Stop lines fix the halt point before crosswalks where walkers always win, arrowed ONLY lanes force the turn, mixed arrows free it, and center lanes serve both-way lefts but never passing [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A03
Reversible lanes flip with rush hours under signals, exclusive bike lanes wall off with solid white, sharrows share the lane, and cars cross bike lanes only to turn when empty [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A04
Yellow curbs refuse parking, diagonal stripes guard obstacles, and fire lanes and safety zones refuse all entry [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A04
Sign colors code red for stop and yield, orange for work, yellow for warning, fluoro for school and walkers, black-white for rules, green for guidance, blue for services and disabled bays, and brown for recreation [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A04
Green guides number east-west even and north-south odd with mile-matched exits, blue-white points to services, and brown-white to scenic and historic sites [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A05
Stop signs demand full halts at lines, walks, or sight points, and all-way stops clear in arrival order with right-side ties broken rightward [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A05
Yield slows for crossing traffic without mandatory halts, entry bans and wrong-way orders reverse mistakes at once, the red slash forbids its picture, and speed, exit-speed, and doubled-zone-fine plates cap pace [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A05
Lane-use plates assign left turns, shared centers, mandatory turns, and right entries that yield to straight-rolling bikes [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A06
Turn bans cover U-turns, side turns, red-light turns, all turns, and forced turns, while one-way, keep-right, and slower-right plates channel flow [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A06
Passing plates forbid or caution overtakes, lane plates reserve bus, carpool, and bike space, and stop plates limit shoulders to emergencies, ban pavement parking, and guard disabled bays [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A07
Yellow diamonds warn ahead of signals, stops, yields, and limit drops, with advisory plates posting curve-safe speeds [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A07
Road-change plates announce two-way returns, merges, lane drops, roundabouts, and divided starts and ends 350 to 500 feet out [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A07
Curve plates for bends, sharp hooks, S-curves, and windings all order slower speeds without passing, and crossroads order left-right scans [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A08
Crossing plates watch side roads, bikes, emergency rigs, trucks, walkers owed slowdowns or halts, and pictured animals by twilight [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A08
Condition plates refuse tall rigs at low spans, flag gravel, soft shoulders, slick bends, waterable dips, tight and single-file bridges, and gear-dropping hills [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A09
Signals bind drivers, walkers, and riders unless officers wave through, and dead lights default to four-way stops [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A09
Reds halt at lines with sensor care, allow right and one-way-left turns absent bans while yielding, yellows urge safe stops, and greens go only through clear boxes with lefts yielding [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A10
Red arrows hold the indicated move with the same turn exceptions, yellow arrows warn of endings, and green arrows free the turn from proper lanes with intersection yields [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A10
Flashing yellow arrows yield turns against green oncoming streams, flashing reds mimic stop signs, and flashing yellows caution through danger, school, and curve points [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A11
Lane signals bar red-X lanes, warn yellowing ones, and free green-arrow lanes under all other rules, while ramp meters hold entries for green [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A12
Work zones slow for signs, flaggers, and officers, orange diamonds flag hazards, channeled stripes lean with travel, arrow boards preview shifts, and vested flaggers wave stop, slow, and go [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A12
Drawbridge reds halt for operating spans, yellows warn of imminent closure, and greens proceed warily [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A13
Flashing drawbridge yellows ready a stop, and gated reds with bells forbid passing around or under at any position [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A13
Walkers start on WALK, never on solid or flashing hands while finishing when caught, heed countdowns as no-start clocks, and push beacons whose flashing halts drivers [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A13
Hybrid beacons clear dark crossings, slow flashing yellows, ready steady yellows, halt steady reds for walkers, and free flashing reds when empty [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A14
Rail approaches slow and never park on steel or inside 15 feet, halting for flashers, gates, flaggers, or visible trains [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A14
Advance signs preview crossings, crossbucks yield with track counts, flashing reds stop at once, gates never bypass, paint marks the halt, and X envelopes flag the strike zone [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A15
Crossers trail stopping buses and trucks, clear every track, fit beyond the far rail first, and never race unbeatable steel [A15].
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A15
School plates demand constant child watch, crossing slowdowns with guard obedience, zone-limit respect under lights and hours, and ready halts for hidden bus stops [A15].
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0065]

items.why: the chapter is a visual vocabulary of signs, markings, and signals tested by recognition, needing its own recognition practice

corpus_stability.reason: The Official Florida Driver License Handbook is a dated revision (rev. 08/2023) reissued at most annually, so traffic control meanings change at most once per year.
